faq: What does this tool calculate?
A delivery fee: base fee + (per-distance rate × trip distance), decomposed so the quote can be shown to the customer.
Is it free to use?
Yes — for setting your own prices or auditing someone else's.
How accurate is the result?
Exact for the tariff entered. Whether the tariff is right is a cost question — check it against your delivery cost per kilometre.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Distance prices the fee; traffic is a cost you absorb or cover with peak policies, not a line in this formula.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Fees are charged on the distance the delivery actually travels — the road figure.
Should distance be one-way or round trip?
The delivery leg is what the customer sees; the return is inside your rate. State the convention and keep it.
Base fee or minimum fee — same thing?
Close cousins: a base fee is the starting part of every price; a minimum fee is a floor under the total. Many tariffs use both.
Should the fee cap at some distance?
Many operators cap and switch to a quote beyond it. The calculator prices the formula's range; the cap is a policy you state.
Free delivery over a threshold?
A marketing layer on this structure: the fee formula still computes what the 'free' delivery costs you, which the threshold should be set from.
Tips and service charges?
Separate lines, separate customs. This formula is the delivery fee itself.
